GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The change follows three observed facts. First, OpenCode 2 runs one background server whose sessions are addressable by every client, so a bot can list, create, prompt, and follow the same sessions a TUI or desktop client uses. Second, Telegram added forum topics inside private chats (Bot API 9.4, 2026-02-09), letting one DM bot host many parallel conversation lanes without a supergroup. Third, the user requires five parallel sessions from a phone. The chosen form is an in-process server plugin because the plugin context already exposes session, event, permission, model, and durable storage surfaces with no separate process, no network authentication, and no password handling. Feature scope was selected feature-by-feature from the mature upstream bot: live status, model switching, interactive questions, message history with revert and fork, subagent activity, file attachments, visibility settings, throttled streaming with a merge window, and corporate connectivity were adopted; agent switching, compaction triggering, worktrees, localization, voice, scheduled tasks, file browsing, and MCP browsing were explicitly rejected by the user. Live status is rendered as a leading emoji in the topic title rather than a pinned or edited status message, following the multiplexer-topic precedent where the title is the cheapest always-visible signal; title edits are throttled because they share the chat rate budget. Delivery correctness invariants are carried over from the abandoned fork's lessons (never two bots on one token, idempotent delivery, restart and replay safety, per-chat throttling) and from the proven vv-chat DM-topic delivery layer: draft streaming with a stable draft id, a durable message mirror map for edit-in-place and exactly-once finals, durable final delivery with boot drain, and a typed fallback to throttled edits.

Alternatives.Alternative: A separate companion process launched by a vvoc telegram start command and connecting over the network client. Rejected by explicit user decision in favor of the in-process plugin; the companion process would add Service.ensure and password handling without any capability the plugin context lacks.

Wrapping or forking the mature upstream Telegram bot. Rejected because it is intentionally single-context, does not implement private-chat topics, and would add a second lifecycle and a second configuration surface outside vvoc; its feature list was instead mined feature-by-feature for what to adopt.

Porting the OpenCode provider from the abandoned ccgram fork, which reads OpenCode's SQLite event log and mirrors it to JSONL behind a multiplexer window identity. Rejected because its upstream maintainer closed the contribution for using a large provider-specific SQLite mirror instead of a small stable boundary, because the log schema is internal and version-fragile, and because it targets OpenCode 1.x rather than the addressable 2.x session API.

Reusing the vv-chat Telegram DM-topic service directly. Its topology and delivery logic is proven in production, but it is coupled to the vv-chat server, repositories, and database, so its patterns (General lane, rotation-free active set, draft and mirror delivery, persisted offset, owner whitelist) are reused rather than its code.

Rendering live status as an edited or pinned status message inside each topic, as the upstream bot does in its single chat. Rejected by user decision in favor of a leading status emoji in the topic title, which is visible from the topic list without opening the topic and costs one throttled edit per state change.
An agent-mode switching surface. Rejected by user decision: the user almost always works through vv-controller, and new sessions inherit their project default agent.
Exposing a compaction trigger. Rejected by user decision: the user never compacts manually, so only context usage is surfaced in /status.

Keeping Telegram state in vvoc.json or in OpenCode's internal tables. Rejected because gateway state is runtime state, not configuration, and coupling it to internal tables repeats the rejected fork's mistake.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Execution deviations recorded for transparency, with no assertion weakened: (1) two repository count tests outside the declared ObservedWriteScope carried hard-coded cardinalities broken by this change (scripts/check-package.test.ts expected eleven plugin subpaths; src/commands/plugin-toggle.test.ts expected thirteen toggle names) and were updated to the new cardinalities; (2) the approved TargetAssertions MustPassCommand referenced the telegram test files with flat src/plugins/telegram.*.test.ts paths that match no files — corrected to the real src/plugins/telegram/*.test.ts paths so the declared gate runs at all; (3) scripts/check-package.ts gained a documented export-name alias for ./plugins/telegram. The approved plan.xml carries only the path correction; this file records every deviation.

The exact status emoji table and the title-edit throttle interval; the draft proposes a small fixed set (running, idle, waiting-question, waiting-permission, error, aborted) with intervals fixed during planning against the chat rate budget.

The exact model picker layout (provider pages, page size, favorites or recency ordering if the native surface exposes them) and whether a bottom reply keyboard is added later; the draft assumes /model inline pages only.
The exact custom-answer flow wording and cancellation path for questions; the draft assumes an explicit custom action that holds the topic input gate until the next plain message or a cancel.
The attachment size and count bounds and the temporary-download location; the draft assumes configurable bounds with explicit rejection notices.
The exact adaptive throttle schedule and merge window duration; the draft bounds edits and coalesces them but leaves exact intervals to planning, informed by the vv-chat delivery implementation.

Scenarios.Scenario: The owner sends /new in General, picks a project from the inline picker, and the plugin creates the native session with the project default agent plus a matching topic titled from the session identity; the owner continues inside that topic.

The owner runs /sync in General after manually deleting some topics; the plugin recreates topics for active sessions and closes topics whose sessions left the 240-minute active window, then reports the counts.

Five sessions run concurrently in five topics; the topic titles carry live status emoji updated through throttled edits, streamed output uses drafts with an edit fallback, and the shared chat rate budget is respected by the adaptive throttle.

A model change is requested with /model in a session topic; the inline picker lists providers and models with the current one marked, the selection is applied through the native session model switch, and /status reflects it.

An agent asks a question mid-run; the topic title shows the waiting-question emoji, the question arrives as inline options plus a custom action, and choosing custom holds the input gate so the next plain message becomes the answer instead of a prompt.

A permission request arrives from a subagent of a bridged session; it is shown as a manual inline-button prompt in that session's topic, the subagent's activity is visible as a card in the same topic, and the owner's decision, or its absence, is reported truthfully.
The owner opens /messages in a topic, picks an earlier message, and forks it; the forked session becomes a new active topic while the original session and topic remain untouched.
The owner sends a photo album with a caption; the bounded attachments are admitted into the prompt together, and an oversized file is rejected with an explicit notice.
The owner sits behind a corporate network that blocks api.telegram.org; a configured custom API root (or outbound proxy, never both) routes Bot API traffic without code changes.

The OpenCode server restarts with opencode service restart; the plugin reloads its durable offset, maps, settings, and bot fingerprint from ctx.storage, resyncs the active set from the native session APIs because the event stream does not replay, and continues without duplicating messages or creating a second General topic.
The bot token environment variable is unset; the gateway disables itself with a value-free diagnostic and starts no polling loop, and the token never appears in a log or in stored state.
